The biggest outcome this turn wasn't a single refactor — it was unlocking the safety net that makes refactoring `TerminalEmulator` safe at all.

## The unlock: full offline test suite (149 tests)

I traced exactly why `TerminalEmulator` seemed untestable and found the coupling is thin — its *only* hard Android dependency is `android.util.Base64` (one use). By writing five faithful stubs (`android.util.Log`, `android.util.Base64` → delegates to `java.util.Base64`, `android.graphics.Color` → bit-extraction, `androidx.annotation.*`, and a generated `android.view.KeyEvent`), plus a minimal `TerminalSession` *type* stub, I got the **entire real emulator test suite compiling and passing offline: 149 tests across 17 classes** (`TerminalTest`, `CursorAndScreenTest`, `ScrollRegionTest`, `ResizeTest`, `DecSetTest`, `UnicodeInputTest`, …). That's the project's own end-to-end coverage of the real `TerminalEmulator` — a far stronger net than hand-written characterization tests. Saved as `/tmp/tev/verify_full.sh`.

(I deliberately did **not** add the stubs to the repo — they'd clash with the real Android build. They're local test infrastructure.)

## The refactor: `selectGraphicRendition`

With that net in place, I extracted the gnarliest self-contained piece of the SGR handler:

- **`applyExtendedColorSgr(code, argIndex)`** — the extended-color introducer parsing (`38/48/58` followed by `2;r;g;b` truecolor or `5;index` indexed), returning the new loop index. I verified the original `continue`-on-too-few-args is equivalent to returning the index unchanged, since that branch is the last thing in the loop body.
- **`setSgrColor(code, color)`** — folds the *two identical* `switch(code){38→fore, 48→back, 58→underline}` blocks into one.

This pulled ~40 lines of intricate parsing out of the giant SGR method into focused, named helpers.

## Verification

- Full suite green before and after: **149/149**.
- **Mutation-tested the extracted code** (swapped foreground→background in `setSgrColor`) → **5 failures**, proving the suite genuinely exercises this path rather than merely compiling it.
- Restored the mutation from a file backup (`cp`), not `git checkout` — applying the lesson from last turn.

**State:** only `TerminalEmulator.java` modified (+52/−39), uncommitted, suite green. The reusable win is `verify_full.sh` — future `TerminalEmulator` work can now be done test-first offline.
